title: Mobile and Portable Command and Control
subtitle: A ten-year programme of specialist command vehicles and rapid-deployment kits, connected by one IP network for live audio, video and data
headline: Mobile and portable IP command centres for overseas government clients, owned across the full life cycle and supported by SciFlair since 2016
photoAlt: Converted command-and-control truck with slide-out operations room
sciflairRole: SciFlair took over service and support of the fleet from 2016, developed SVMS over the same period, and in 2019 proposed a Phase 2 upgrade that the client approved but did not proceed with after COVID-19, when government priorities changed
need: A government client needed to collect, monitor and record audio, video and data from many sources at an incident, and pass it in real time to headquarters for decisions and analysis.

Two operational teams had to work the same way: one moving as a convoy of specialist vehicles, the other carrying the same capability in rugged portable cases that can be set up anywhere without specialist knowledge. Separate camera, radio and recording systems had to come under one common platform.
role: XAD Communications was the prime contractor and design authority across the whole life cycle, from concept and requirements through architecture, design, manufacture, factory and site acceptance, deployment and in-service support to final retirement. The programme was led technically by the engineer who went on to found SciFlair: he wrote the technical proposals, negotiated at director and government level, and directed XAD's four engineering groups (audio, video, data and RF), 22 engineers in total.
built: Team 1, mobile: a convoy of eight converted vehicles, comprising a main operator vehicle, two auxiliary vehicles, and retransmission, transcriber, communication, intelligent and photo vehicles

Team 2, portable: the same functions as stations in precision-fabricated Pelican cases, including a main operator station, retransmission, transcriber and photo stations, and portable operations rooms
35 rapidly deployable camera and communication kits across both teams, including mobile cameras on pneumatic masts
Vehicle conversions from 4x4s and vans up to 18-tonne trucks, with operator workstations, an on-board generator and battery bank, stabilising legs, air-conditioning and networking racks
An end-to-end IP network across wired and wireless links, carrying live and recorded audio, video and data between kits, vehicles and headquarters
Portable kits with a 5 GHz wireless link, a Wi-Fi access point for nearby viewers, an industrial touchscreen for camera control and up to 8 hours on battery
XAD's own XVMS video management software, later succeeded by SciFlair's SVMS
builtScope: Two teams, eight specialist vehicles, a full portable equivalent in Pelican cases, and 35 deployable camera and communication kits, all on one IP network.

delivery.title: Concept and requirements
delivery.text: Operational needs for both teams were captured and turned into the technical proposals and system requirements.

delivery.title: Architecture and design
delivery.text: One IP architecture for vehicles, portable stations and kits, so every unit can work alone or as part of the wider deployment.

delivery.title: Production and verification
delivery.text: Vehicle conversions and Pelican-case systems manufactured and integrated, with factory acceptance testing before shipment.

delivery.title: Validation and deployment
delivery.text: Site acceptance and field testing in operational conditions, where the system exceeded the client's expectations.

delivery.title: Change control
delivery.text: Scope changes over the programme were managed by agreeing priorities for critical deliverables, holding budget and schedule.

delivery.title: Support and retirement
delivery.text: In-service support for a decade, with SciFlair taking over service and support from 2016, until the programme closed in 2019.

results.label: specialist vehicles in the mobile team

nextGen.title: What came next
nextGen.text: The programme's lessons shaped SciFlair's SVMS video management software, rewritten from the ground up from 2016. In 2019 SciFlair proposed a Phase 2 upgrade, which the client approved; it did not go ahead after COVID-19, when government priorities changed.
